title: The Same Skill in PowerShell
description: The Windows version of the same install: create the skill directory with New-Item and write SKILL.md from a here-string.

steps.description: This is the Windows, PowerShell version of the same install. It writes the identical `SKILL.md` into the skill directory under `.agents`, and the file is the same either way; only the directory changes.
`New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path .agents\skills\commit-message` creates the directory, `-Force` tolerates one that already exists, and `| Out-Null` suppresses its output.
`Set-Content -Path .agents\skills\commit-message\SKILL.md -Encoding utf8` writes the file as UTF-8 from the here-string that starts at `@'`.
The front matter is the same: `name: commit-message`, and the `description` that states when to use it.
The body repeats the same instruction: read the staged files with `git status --short`, write a subject line under seventy characters, and add the reasoning only if it is not obvious.

steps.question: The page says the description is the trigger, so a description naming what works, while one naming the topic does not?
